content: If you suspect an overdose and the individual is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). For non-emergency situations, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Before starting this medication and during its use, laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., liver and kidney function tests) may be required to monitor your condition and ensure the medication's safety. It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. If the medication bottle includes a desiccant (a moisture-absorbing agent), keep it in the bottle. Ensure the bottle is tightly closed when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Common side effects of this medication may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, constipation, headache, or joint/muscle pain. Occasionally, you may notice whole or partial tablets/capsules in your stool. If this occurs frequently, inform your doctor. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, mesalamine may worsen ulcerative colitis. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not a complete list of potential side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking mesalamine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other aminosalicylates (e.g., balsalazide, olsalazine), salicylates (e.g., aspirin, salsalate), sulfasalazine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may increase your sensitivity to the sun, particularly if you have skin conditions such as atopic dermatitis or eczema. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. This medication is similar to aspirin. Children and teenagers under 18 years of age should not take aspirin or aspirin-related medications (e.g., salicylates) if they have chickenpox, the flu, an undiagnosed illness, or have recently received a vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Mesalamine is very similar to balsalazide, olsalazine, and sulfasalazine. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., urine normetanephrine levels), potentially causing false test results.
